newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply off after setting 2-mth low.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply off after setting 2-mth low.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended heavily depressed on Friday after plummeting to a two-month low during the session as investors continued to unwind positions and search for better value elsewhere, analysts said.

The Hang Seng Index closed on a loss of 126.69 points, or 0.96 percent, at 13,113.26, capping a week of heavy losses. The blue-chip index gave up 547.24 points or 4.01 percent this week, its biggest weekly point loss since March 1996.
"The market needs a consolidation. It moved up so much and many investors who bought earlier have enjoyed good profits," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
"When they saw strong resistance at 14,000 they moved the money to other markets," he said.
The Hang Seng hit a record high of 14,004.93 on January 16.

"This is only temporary -- a kind of consolidation after the index reached 14,000," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International. "Some fund managers have decided that other markets in the region are more attractive so you are seeing rotational buying and selling."
He said some investors were finding Singapore attractive.
Friday's low of 12,962.15 was the lowest level reached by the index since December 19.
Turnover was HK$10.49 billion compared with HK$8.71 billion on Thursday.
"We are going to see further consolidation probably for another week before it resumes its uptrend again," said Tang. He said the Hang Seng Index should find support at 12,800 points.
"I think the uptrend is still intact so far," he added.
Conglomerates were hit hard on Friday.
Swire Pacific dropped HK$2.25 to HK$65.25, Wheelock fell HK$0.70 to HK$19.90 and Hutchison slumped HK$0.75 to HK$56.25.
Among the banks, HSBC fell HK$2.50 to HK$183.50.

Losses in the property sector were smaller than in other industry groups. Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$0.25 to HK$89.00, Henderson Land was unchanged at HK$69.00 and Cheung Kong fell HK$0.25 to HK$71.75.

Stock futures in Cheung Kong, HSBC and Hongkong Telecom registered their first trading volume in nearly a year following the launch of the Hong Kong Futures Exchange automated trading system on Friday. Twenty-three contracts traded on HSBC March futures, seven on Hongkong Telecom and two on Cheung Kong.
February Hang Seng Index futures rose 20 points to 13,140.
